overall_summary: Crypto gets a lift from fresh SEC approvals for leveraged Bitcoin and Ether products plus progress on custody rules, while soft jobs data and Fed patience cut rate-hike odds and support risk assets. Geopolitical strikes near oil infrastructure add some inflation caution, yet the G7 oil release helps offset that pressure. Overall tone favors Bitcoin on regulatory and macro tailwinds.
key_points: SEC clears first 3x leveraged BTC and ETH ETPs
Soft jobs data slashes October Fed hike odds
Fed officials signal patience, markets price pause
G7 coordinates 100 million barrel oil release
Oil and Hormuz risks keep inflation watch active

items.title: SEC Clears First US 3x Leveraged Bitcoin and Ether ETPs
items.summary: The SEC approved a Cboe BZX rule change on October 2 letting Volatility Shares list 3x daily Bitcoin and Ether ETPs alongside gold, silver, oil and gas products. These futures-based vehicles reset leverage every day and still need an effective S-1 before trading starts. Traders should care because this is the first triple-leveraged US crypto product set, expanding tools for directional bets and signaling regulators now treat BTC and ETH more like traditional commodities. It could pull in more volume and sophisticated flow once live.
items.impact: More leveraged products and trading volume once S-1 clears

items.title: SEC Proposes Crypto Custody Rules for Advisers and Funds
items.summary: On October 1 the SEC proposed modernizing custody rules so registered advisers and funds can hold crypto assets more easily, including limited self-custody when no qualified custodian is available and allowing state-chartered trust companies as custodians. Chair Atkins framed it as giving a clear compliant path where none existed. This matters for traders because it lowers barriers for big institutions and wealth managers to allocate directly into Bitcoin and other crypto, potentially unlocking steadier demand beyond ETFs.
items.impact: Easier institutional custody could drive sustained inflows

items.title: Weak Jobs Data Sparks BTC Spike to $87K Then Long Liquidations
items.summary: September nonfarm payrolls came in at just 29,000 versus roughly 90,000 expected, unemployment ticked to 4.2 percent, and Fed pause odds jumped. Bitcoin ripped toward 87,000 before rejecting hard, triggering around 433 million dollars in liquidations, mostly longs. Price has since stabilized and reclaimed 85,000 on the weekend. Traders care because the macro tailwind is real yet the technical rejection and leverage flush show the market remains fragile near resistance; next move hinges on whether 85k holds as support.
items.impact: Dovish macro vs unresolved resistance and washed leverage

items.title: IMF Disburses $138M to El Salvador After Bitcoin Waivers
items.summary: The IMF completed reviews of El Salvador’s 1.4 billion dollar program and released about 138 million dollars, granting waivers for Bitcoin accumulation breaches. The country committed to no further public-sector Bitcoin buys beyond documented private donations and to keep reducing state involvement in crypto. This is relevant because it keeps a high-profile sovereign Bitcoin holder funded while capping official accumulation, tempering the nation-state adoption narrative without forcing sales of existing holdings.
items.impact: Limits new sovereign buying but normalizes existing holdings

items.title: Miners’ AI Pivot Costs Estimated $1.5B in Hashrate Hardware
items.summary: Public Bitcoin miners shed roughly 75 EH/s of realized hashrate in the first half of 2026 while shifting power and sites toward AI and high-performance computing. At an assumed 20 dollars per terahash that equates to about 1.5 billion dollars in mining gear, with over a billion already written down in impairments. Traders should watch this because sustained hashrate migration can slow network growth and alter miner selling pressure, even as the companies diversify revenue away from pure Bitcoin production.
items.impact: Potential hashrate drag offset by miner financial diversification

items.title: Bitget Tops Protection Fund Back to 3,705 BTC After Hack
items.summary: Bitget used company funds to restore its user protection fund to 3,705 BTC, valued around 316 million dollars, after the late-September roughly 387 million dollar hot-wallet breach attributed by Chainalysis to North Korea-linked actors. Reserves sit at a 131 percent ratio across major assets and withdrawals have been resuming in phases. This restores confidence in a large exchange’s backstop, but the episode and AI-traced laundering keep security and counterparty risk front of mind for anyone parking size on centralized platforms.
items.impact: Exchange resilience restored; security risks remain elevated

items.title: Soft September Jobs Report Slashes October Fed Hike Odds
items.summary: US nonfarm payrolls rose just 29,000 in September, far below the 80 to 90 thousand expected, while unemployment ticked up to 4.2 percent and prior months were revised lower. Wage growth also cooled. Traders now see only about a 20 percent chance of a rate hike at the late October FOMC meeting, down sharply from earlier in the week. Crypto traders should care because reduced near-term tightening pressure typically supports risk assets like Bitcoin by easing financial conditions.
items.impact: Supports risk-on move in BTC and equities short-term

items.title: Fed Officials Stress Patience, Markets Price October Pause
items.summary: New York Fed President John Williams and Vice Chair Philip Jefferson both signaled no urgency for another rate increase, saying the Fed can take time to assess more data after the September hike. This followed the soft jobs numbers and earlier cooler inflation prints. Odds of an October move collapsed. For traders this confirms the path of least resistance is a hold at the October 27-28 meeting, which is generally constructive for Bitcoin until the next major data hits.
items.impact: Lowers immediate policy risk for crypto markets

items.title: US 10-Year Yields Hold Near Multi-Decade Highs
items.summary: Despite the weak jobs report, the 10-year Treasury yield stayed elevated around 5.25 to 5.28 percent after briefly dipping, having hit levels not seen since 2002 earlier in the week. Drivers include sticky energy prices from geopolitical tensions, heavy Treasury supply, and rising term premium. Crypto traders need to watch this closely because persistently high long-end yields keep real rates restrictive and can cap risk appetite even if the Fed pauses.
items.impact: Sustains pressure on valuations and liquidity-sensitive assets

items.title: Dollar Index Holds Near 17-Month Highs After Soft Data
items.summary: The DXY closed the week near 102 after a third straight weekly gain, though it eased slightly following the jobs miss as rate-hike bets faded. Strength has been supported by yield differentials and safe-haven flows amid global bond market stress. A firm dollar remains a headwind for Bitcoin historically, so traders should monitor whether the post-NFP dip extends or buyers defend the recent highs heading into next week’s data.
items.impact: Mixed near-term; strong DXY still a drag if it rebounds

items.title: ISM Services PMI Due Monday as Next Key Macro Test
items.summary: No major US data dropped on Sunday, but markets turn immediately to the ISM Non-Manufacturing or Services PMI on Monday October 5 at 10 a.m. Eastern. Consensus sits near 55.7 after a solid prior reading. Services dominate the economy, so a strong print could revive growth concerns and support the dollar and yields, while a miss would reinforce the cooling narrative from jobs. This is the first high-impact release of the new week for crypto positioning.
items.impact: Potential volatility catalyst depending on beat or miss

items.title: Elevated Oil and Geopolitics Keep Inflation Risks Alive
items.summary: Even with cooler labor data, markets remain focused on energy prices and Middle East tensions that have pushed oil higher and complicated the inflation outlook. This is a key reason long yields and the dollar have stayed supported despite fading October hike odds. Crypto traders should treat this as an unresolved risk: softer growth data is bullish for risk assets, but any renewed oil spike could quickly reprice the Fed path higher again before the October 28 meeting.
items.impact: Keeps upside inflation risk and rate uncertainty in play

items.title: Houthis Claim Missile-Drone Hit on Aramco Near Riyadh
items.summary: Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis say they struck an Aramco facility south of Riyadh with ballistic missiles and drones, and videos showed fire and heavy smoke at the site. Saudi coalition officials called the claim misleading and said they hit Houthi targets in Sanaa and elsewhere. Traders should care because any credible threat to Saudi oil infrastructure raises the risk premium on crude just as markets reopen, feeding inflation fears and risk-off pressure.
items.impact: Oil spike risk and broader risk-asset pressure into the week open

items.title: Brazil Votes in Knife-Edge Lula vs Flavio Bolsonaro Race
items.summary: Brazilians are at the polls today in the first round of a polarized presidential election pitting leftist incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva against right-wing senator Flavio Bolsonaro, son of the jailed former president. Polls point to a tight race and a likely October 25 runoff, with big stakes for Latin America, U.S. and China trade ties, and commodity policy. Crypto and EM traders should watch because Brazil is a major risk barometer and any surprise first-round outcome or chaos could swing the real and global risk sentiment.
items.impact: EM and commodity risk premium hinged on unresolved first-round result

items.title: Russia Hits Kyiv Bridge as German Chancellor Merz Visits
items.summary: A Russian drone struck Kyiv's Northern Bridge for a second straight day just as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz arrived on a surprise solidarity visit with Zelensky. Merz is expected to lock in more than a billion dollars in new military support plus energy repair funds and drone interceptors. For markets this keeps the Ukraine war premium alive and signals Europe is still deepening commitments rather than winding them down.
items.impact: Sustained Europe risk premium and defense-spending narrative

items.title: Another Tanker Struck Near Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: UK maritime authorities reported another crude tanker hit by an unidentified projectile east of Oman, with the crew safe and no major spill. Iranian media claim multiple tanker strikes in recent days even as Washington insists the strait is effectively open under escort. Energy traders care because repeated hits keep the Hormuz risk premium sticky and can reprice oil, freights, and inflation expectations the moment futures reopen.
items.impact: Persistent chokepoint risk supporting higher oil and volatility

items.title: G7 Starts Coordinated 100 Million Barrel Oil Release
items.summary: G7 leaders agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil and diesel from strategic stocks over four months via the IEA, with a front-loaded diesel tranche in the first 20 days. The move came after U.S. pressure over record diesel prices and aims to cool fuel costs without export bans among members. For crypto and risk assets this is a near-term counter to energy-driven inflation, potentially easing rate-hike fears if the barrels actually hit the market.
items.impact: Downward pressure on diesel and oil prices, supportive for risk appetite

items.title: North Korea Fires Hypersonic Intermediate-Range Missile
items.summary: Kim Jong Un oversaw a Saturday launch of what Pyongyang called a hypersonic intermediate-range strategic missile that state media said hit a target about 1,000 kilometers away in the East Sea. South Korea and Japan tracked a long-range ballistic flight amid already elevated tensions after recent DMZ landmine incidents. Asia risk and defense names may react, but the test is unlikely to dominate global risk assets unless it triggers a sharper U.S.-allied response.
items.impact: Localized Asia security premium, limited immediate global risk move
